reason: I'll clear the broken fragments first so the wound is ready for repair.
expectation: The white blood cells will remove debris around the clot, though the skin gap will probably remain.

alternatives.reason: A new blood vessel also supports healing, but clearing the wound seems like a useful place to start.

effect: The debris is cleared, but the surface gap remains. I can now prepare the parts needed for repair.
reaction: It makes sense that the white blood cells engulfed the fragments.
reason: I'll prepare replacement skin cells to help close the surface gap.
expectation: The cells will use the supplied materials and energy to make more skin cells, though I don't know exactly how they'll be added to the wound.

alternatives.reason: A new blood vessel could supply the healing tissue, but I want to address the open surface first.

effect: The new cells are ready at the wound edge, but the gap is still open.
reaction: The outline makes their next placement clear.
reason: I'll add the new cells to the cleared wound to close its surface.
expectation: The new cells will spread over the gap; the wound may still need support and a blood supply.

alternatives.reason: A new vessel should help supply the repair, but the surface cells are ready to place now.

effect: The surface is closed, but the deeper tissue still needs strengthening and a blood supply.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the cells span the gap, though repair isn't finished.
reason: I'll prepare supporting fibres to help strengthen the tissue beneath the closed surface.
expectation: The skin cells will use the amino acids to make supporting protein fibres, which can then be added to the wound.

alternatives.reason: The new blood vessel is also needed, but I'll build the support first.

effect: The supporting fibres are ready, but the deeper gap still needs them.
reaction: The outlines make it clear where the fibres belong.
reason: I'll add the fibres to strengthen the tissue beneath the new skin.
expectation: The fibres will join the surviving tissue across the deeper gap; a blood supply may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The new vessel is also needed, but the fibres are ready to place now.

effect: The fibres now support part of the deeper wound, but the blood supply still needs attention.
reaction: The repair is coming together, though the deeper wound isn't fully rebuilt yet.
reason: I'll follow the only available combination to prepare a new blood vessel.
expectation: The wound messengers will prompt a branch to grow from the nearby capillary, which may then supply the repair.

effect: The capillary has grown a branch toward the wound, ready to add to the repair.
reaction: The branch makes the blood-supply step clearer.
reason: I'll follow the only available combination and add the sprout to the wound.
expectation: The new vessel will connect with the wound's blood supply and help support the healing tissue.

effect: The new vessel connects to another vessel, supplying the repaired tissue; the temporary clot now needs clearing.
reaction: Seeing blood flow through the joined vessels makes their purpose clear.
reason: I'll follow the only available combination to clear the temporary clot.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the clot's protein threads, leaving the repaired tissue in place.

effect: Most clot threads are gone, while the new fibres and capillaries remain. The wound is closed, though the scar will keep changing.
reaction: The small scar makes the repair feel more realistic than the skin simply returning to its original state.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the capillary sprout was worthwhile because seeing it connect and carry blood showed how the repaired tissue gets supplies.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the supporting fibres and then fitting them felt a little repetitive after doing the same two-stage process with the skin cells, although their purpose was clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the clot was mostly cleared after it had protected the wound, leaving a scar that keeps changing.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt entirely arbitrary. I followed the named pairing for wound messengers and the capillary; the picture suggested a growing branch, but didn't explain exactly how the message caused it.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing the wound close and regain a blood supply made the connected steps interesting, though the repeated make-and-fit pattern could get tiring.
